title: Chuck Person’s Eccojams Vol. 1 cassette
lede: Daniel Lopatin’s 2010 cassette of slowed loops, packaged to look like the box of the 1993 game Ecco the Dolphin.
summary: Proto-vaporwave cassette whose J-card borrows the Ecco the Dolphin game box. 2010.

evidence.note: Relies on Wikipedia. The only image found was a 599 × 383 J-card scan in the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release/88ba5807-ba5d-41a5-bcff-14dc672688e3/cover-art), below the size needed to observe it.

styles.note: A precursor: Wikipedia credits it and Far Side Virtual with the musical template, and its game-box packaging set the habit of quoting 1990s consumer products. Partial fit, because it has none of the later pastel palette.

context: Released in August 2010 on cassette by The Curatorial Club. Wikipedia: “With packaging that resembled the 1993 video game Ecco the Dolphin, the album inspired a host of suburban teens and young adults to formulate what would become vaporwave.” [Wikipedia: Vaporwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporwave).
Lopatin had released several of the loops earlier on YouTube as sunsetcorp, from his audio-visual album Memory Vague (2009). [Wikipedia: Vaporwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaporwave).
interpretation: The packaging is appropriation of a specific commercial object, not a new graphic language. That act of quoting a mass-market product is what the style kept.

rights.statement: Copyrighted packaging that reuses Sega game artwork. No image is stored here.
